text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — node gpu-pool-7 ephemeral storage > 92% and multiple pods evicted (modelcache, runtime). Alert ID PD-4882. Auto-assigned to @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. quick check: which pods were evicted? any customer-facing routes impacted?

maria: saw a stream of kubelet evict logs earlier: modelcache-* pods killed, then some runtime pods restarted and failed CUDA init. Customers hitting higher 5xx on inference endpoints (~10m spike).

ajay: copying relevant kubelet log tail:

```
Jul 28 03:12:45 kubelet kubelet[1]: eviction: pod "modelcache-7" - ephemeral-storage usage exceeded threshold, deleting
Jul 28 03:12:46 kubelet kubelet[1]: eviction: pod "runtime-562" - oom_kill process 4321 (serve)
Jul 28 03:12:47 kubelet kubelet[1]: container runtime restart: pod runtime-562 -> CrashLoopBackOff
```

lee: and runtime logs show CUDA init failures after restart:

```
2026-07-28T03:13:02Z ERROR serve: failed to init cuda context: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-07-28T03:13:02Z ERROR runtime: worker exited: runtime crash: failed to mmap kv cache
```

eng-runtime: That mmap error smells like model cache corruption after sudden eviction. When the model cache was deleted from disk the runtime tries to rebuild and spikes IO and then hits CUDA OOM trying to reload warm-in GPU memory.

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: (1) cordon gpu-pool-7 to stop new pods scheduling, (2) drain non-critical pods, (3) remove partially-written cache shards from /var/lib/modelcache, (4) restart modelcache as single replica with reduced memory prefetch, (5) temporarily shift traffic away from affected nodes via routing rule. Thoughts?

maria: agree. also we should increase eviction thresholds for ephemeral storage class on that node group to avoid cascade while we recover. we have tight logrotate gaps on some runtime pods — large logs ate disk.

ajay: running commands now:

```
# cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-pool-7
# drain non-critical
kubectl drain node/gpu-pool-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --pod-selector='role!=critical'
```

olivia: customer-ops: we need a short ~10m notice to customers in the affected region. impact: intermittent 5xx on generation endpoints, fallback to lower-tier models working but higher latency. ETA for mitigation ~30-45m. Can you post?

customer-ops: posting now to status page (internal draft):

"We are investigating increased errors and latency for inference in us-west-2. Root cause appears to be node ephemeral storage pressure causing pod evictions and subsequent model reload failures. Engineers are actively mitigating — routing traffic away and restoring model cache. We will update in 30 minutes or on resolution."

eng-runtime: ops update — I removed corrupted cache shards and started a single modelcache pod on a healthy node with flags: `--prefetch=0 --cache-writeback=off`. That reduces IO while we warm the KV cache.

sre-oncall: good. verify node disk usage after cleanup:

```
ssh node@gpu-pool-7
sudo du -sh /var/lib/modelcache/* | sort -h
# after cleanup: /var/lib/modelcache total 4.3G (was ~86G)
```

maria: observed modelcache pod now `Running` and runtime pods are slowly recovering. we still see a few CUDA OOMs on older runtimes that tried to reload multiple models in parallel. throttling restarts: set env var `MODEL_LOAD_PARALLELISM=1` on runtime for the temporarily deployed ReplicaSet.

eng-runtime: applying change to deployment: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime MODEL_LOAD_PARALLELISM=1 --namespace=prod` — will roll through canary 10% then 50%. fallback policy is already set to alternate-model-2 which is lower capacity but stable.

sre-oncall: routing change executed: Traffic for model:default/gpt-large shifted off gpu-pool-7 to gpu-pool-3,4 via the router. Hit-rate on 5xx is dropping from 7% -> 1.2% in the last 6m.

olivia: status update posted to customers. keeping them on shorter model list until we confirm cache stability. any risk of data loss?

maria: no customer data lost — this is ephemeral local cache only. We've audited disk writes; model artifacts come from persistent model store.

ajay: follow-up actions tracked:
- increase nodegroup ephemeral eviction threshold from 85% -> 93% (temporary)
- audit runtime logrotate configs and tighten retention for modelcache/runtime logs
- add a pre-drain hook to gracefully checkpoint KV caches where possible
- add alert to detect sudden modelcache footprint growth > 10GB in 5m

sre-oncall: I'm going to hand off to night oncall in 45m. current state: degraded but stable, routing mitigations in place, modelcache warm-up ongoing. Will create incident postmortem ticket PD-4882 with initial timeline.

eng-runtime: note for postmortem: consider modelcache store on separate non-ephemeral disk (local SSD or network-attached PV) for nodes with hot workloads, and limit local log writes by moving verbose debug to a remote logger.

customer-ops: final customer update queued: "We reduced routing to limit impact and restarted core services — errors are resolved for most customers. We continue to monitor and will follow up with details."

sre-oncall: handing over to @lee (night-oncall) for watch. I'll attach relevant logs and the cleanup commands in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

lee: ACK, I'll monitor for any re-eviction and keep pages open. If we see >2% 5xx sustained, I'll escalate to SEV and bring in hardware infra.

maria: thanks everyone — nice quick coordination. closing channel for new action items; add any follow-ups to PD-4882.
